fdroid:app.subster.name: Subster
fdroid:app.subster.summary: Music timeline party game that plays songs from your own Subsonic library
fdroid:app.subster.description:
Subster is a pass-and-play music party game for your own music collection. A mystery song plays blind — no title, no artist, no year. Your job: place it on your timeline by guessing whether it came out before or after the songs you already hold. Guess right and you keep the card. First to 10 cards wins.
It works like the card game Hitster, but with no physical cards, no accounts, and no backend: the app talks directly to your Subsonic-compatible music server (Navidrome, Airsonic, Gonic, …).
 Features 
 Plays your music — connects to any Subsonic-compatible server
 Save several servers and switch between them; each remembers its own library and playlist
 Smart deck building: songs are ranked by real-world recognizability (Deezer popularity + a bundled canon of chart hits), so the deck feels fair instead of obscure
 Original release years via MusicBrainz and Wikidata — a remaster from 2015 still counts as its original year
 Tokens: skip a song, bet against another player's placement and steal the card, or earn a bonus for naming title and artist
 Difficulty presets, year range and genre filters, clip length options
 Keeps playing with the screen off (lock-screen media controls)
 English and German UI
 Privacy 
No accounts, no ads, no analytics. To rank songs and resolve years, only artist/title of library songs are sent to the public Deezer, MusicBrainz and Wikidata APIs — nothing about you or your server. The "Online metadata" setting has three levels: full, "No Deezer" (drops the only proprietary service but keeps MusicBrainz/Wikidata years), and offline, where only your own server is contacted.
You need a Subsonic-compatible music server to play. Your server credentials never leave the device, and are stored as a salted token rather than the password itself — except for servers that only accept legacy authentication, where the app tells you that the password has to be kept.

fdroid:ca.asmat.foggymaps.name: Foggy Maps
fdroid:ca.asmat.foggymaps.summary: A personal exploration map where fog dissipates where you have walked.
fdroid:ca.asmat.foggymaps.description:
Foggy Maps is a personal exploration map. The whole world starts hidden under a semi-transparent violet fog; as you physically move, the fog dissipates along your path, permanently, with soft dithered edges. The filled-in map becomes a lifetime record of where you have been.
It is not a social network. Your location data stays on your device and moves only where you explicitly send it. Logging, fog clearing and rendering all work offline, and the app asks for nothing on first launch: the map opens fogged, and each permission is requested at the moment you switch the feature on.
Features:
* Live GPS fog clearing on a pixel-art top-down map. The reveal radius follows the fix's own reported accuracy, nudged by the terrain under it, so a precise fix marks a small disc and a vague one is thrown away.
* Dithered gradient fog drawn by a GPU shader, pixel-locked at every zoom.
* Raw track points and a per-tile heatmap stored locally in SQLite. The heatmap is a cache the app can throw away and rebuild from the points.
* A dated stamp for the first visit to each city, region and country, collected in a scrapbook passport beside the landmarks and badges you have found.
* Cleared ground counts as XP up a ladder of real-world landmarks, rewarding new ground only: no streaks, no daily-engagement pressure.
* Photos pin to a spot, clear the fog around them, and sit on the map as thumbnails.
* Import GPX or Google Timeline history. Export GPX or a full JSON backup.
* Optional WebDAV backup to your own Nextcloud, on startup, daily and on demand. Off until you configure a server.
* Landmark and badge packs are plain JSON, loadable at runtime with no app update.
Online OpenStreetMap data (the OpenFreeMap basemap, Overpass for terrain and place names) is on by default and can be turned off in settings; with it off, the app makes no network requests. While it is on, the app fetches public map data for the area you visit, which discloses your rough location to those servers, and caches it on the device. Both endpoints can be pointed at a server of your own.
Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, licensed under the Open Database Licence.

fdroid:cityfreqs.com.pilfershushjammer.name: PilferShush Jammer
fdroid:cityfreqs.com.pilfershushjammer.summary: Block unwanted use of onboard microphone
fdroid:cityfreqs.com.pilfershushjammer.description:
Features a passive jammer technique that engages the microphone thereby
blocking other apps from using it. But does NOT listen to or record any of the
audio from the microphone. It uses 0% CPU and no noticeable battery use. However
is not intended to be left on permanently due to the variety of triggers that
can cause audio_focus_state changes (VOIP etc).
Also features an active jammer that emits tones constrained to the NUHF
range of 18 kHz to 24 kHz range. User determined carrier frequency and drift
limits with rate for random tone emissions depending on the device capabilities.
For instance 20000 Hz carrier, drift limit 1000 Hz and rate slow - will output
random frequency between 19 kHz and 21 kHz approximately every second.
Audible artifacts are present during the NUHF tones but this may be changed in a
future release. Experimental white noise output may not be very effective at
blocking and is a somewhat annoying sound. The device speaker output may not
have enough amplitude to block unwanted NUHF signals - testing will determine.
* Manual start
* Notification post when running
* Auto stop and restart when telephony interrupts
* Currently relies on audio_focus_state changes for auto-switching
* Active jammer

fdroid:com.cairnlabworks.okanzo.name: Okanzo
fdroid:com.cairnlabworks.okanzo.summary: Private, offline-first net worth tracker with on-device encryption
fdroid:com.cairnlabworks.okanzo.description:
Okanzo is a private, offline-first Android app for tracking your net worth - your assets minus your liabilities - organised into portfolios.
Your financial data is stored encrypted on your device and never leaves it, except when you deliberately export an encrypted backup.
Features:
* Track stocks, funds, crypto, gold, cash, bank deposits, property, vehicles, bonds, and more.
* Fetch current prices for market-linked assets by ticker symbol.
* Select stock exchanges across the US, China, Europe, Japan, Hong Kong, and India, and save a preferred-exchange shortlist.
* Look up full Yahoo Finance tickers for other markets and cryptocurrency pairs.
* Track loans, mortgages, credit cards, pending payments, and taxes.
* See total assets, liabilities, and net worth in the Quiet overview, with separate Assets and Liabilities tabs.
* Optionally shorten the net-worth headline with currency-specific units, including lakh/crore for INR.
* Create and switch between multiple portfolios.
* Reorder categories and individual items.
* Convert holdings using cached exchange rates.
* Encrypt the local database with SQLCipher and protect its key with Android Keystore.
* Optionally lock the app with fingerprint or device credentials.
* Export and import password-protected encrypted backups.
* Use the sage light theme or deep-green Midnight dark theme, or follow your device. Wallpaper colors are available in light mode on Android 12+.
* Find preferences in grouped settings and enter holdings with focused forms and optional notes.
* See release highlights after updating, or reopen them from Settings. App information has its own About dialog.
* Choose from 21 app languages in Settings, or follow your device language.
Okanzo is offline-first. Network access is only used to look up public market prices and exchange rates. Only a ticker symbol or base currency code is sent. There are no accounts, analytics, or trackers, and portfolio values, names, and holdings are never transmitted.
Note on network use: currency exchange rates are refreshed automatically in the background - on first launch and then at most once every 12 hours - so your net worth is always shown correctly in your chosen base currency. Market prices, by contrast, are only fetched when you explicitly refresh or tap fetch-price on an asset.

fdroid:com.dessalines.thumbkey.name: Thumb-Key
fdroid:com.dessalines.thumbkey.summary: A privacy-conscious keyboard made for your thumbs.
fdroid:com.dessalines.thumbkey.description:
Thumb-Key is a privacy-conscious smart keyboard, made specifically for your thumbs.
It features a 3x3 grid layout , and uses swipes for the less common letters. Its easy to learn, and designed for fast typing speeds.
Instead of relying on profit-driven, privacy-offending word and sentence prediction for accuracy, as do most popular phone keyboards like Gboard and Swiftkey, Thumb-Key uses large keys with predictable positions , to prevent your eyes from hunting and pecking for letters.
As the key positions get ingrained into your muscle memory, eventually you'll be able to appromixate the fast speeds of touch-typing, your eyes never having to leave the text edit area.
This project is a follow-up to the now unmaintained (and closed-source) MessagEase Keyboard , which is its main inspiration.

This application is not a standalone program. It is a front end client to use

fdroid:com.tallydigital.oomdroid.name: Orion Master
fdroid:com.tallydigital.oomdroid.summary: Native 1oom port of Master of Orion (1993). Requires your own LBX files
fdroid:com.tallydigital.oomdroid.description:
Orion Master is a native Android port of 1oom, the GPLv2 reimplementation of Master of Orion (1993).
This app is the engine and a touch-friendly shell only. It does not include, download, or redistribute the original game's LBX data files. It cannot run without a legally owned Master of Orion v1.3 LBX set, which is proprietary.
On first launch, tap Choose LBX folder. The system folder picker opens. Pick the folder that contains fonts.lbx. A complete v1.3 set also needs V11.LBX (the 1.3 patch). The app copies the files into its private storage.
The classic 1993 interface is drawn letterboxed in landscape. Taps are mapped to mouse clicks. Extra on-screen controls appear for long lists, and the Android keyboard is shown when the game asks for text.
The app is offline. It has no internet permission, no ads, and no analytics.
This build is intended for F-Droid. It is not published on Google Play, because the APK cannot run as a complete game without user-supplied data.
Source: the 1oom engine remains in the upstream src/ tree. Android-specific code lives under app/.

fdroid:de.huepping.wortmuehle.name: Wortmühle
fdroid:de.huepping.wortmuehle.summary: Daily German word puzzle — 9 or 8 letters, one pangram, fully offline
fdroid:de.huepping.wortmuehle.description:
Wortmühle ("word mill") is a daily German word puzzle: build as many German words as you can from nine (or eight) letters on the 3×3 mill board. Every word must use the center letter, and every puzzle contains at least one pangram — a word using all the letters.
Features:
• One new puzzle every day, with the last seven days replayable
• Two daily puzzles: 9 and 8 letters — 2500 nine-letter and 3000 eight-letter puzzles built in, fully offline
• Scoring with own letter values (1–4), with a pangram bonus
• Tap a found word for its definition — bundled, no network needed
• Light/dark mode selectable (follows the system otherwise)
• No permissions, no tracking, no ads, no accounts, no Google services
The app requests no permissions at all and never touches the network. The definitions ship with it: they come from de.wiktionary.org, are licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and are shortened to the first two senses. Each definition carries a link to its Wiktionary page — tapping it opens your browser.
Note: the game and its vocabulary are entirely in German. The word list is derived from free sources (igerman98 word list, de.wiktionary, OpenSubtitles frequency data).

 Haptic feedback on every answer, fully usable offline.
 Designed for children: no account, no network access, no analytics, no ads. Everything stays on the device.
 Made by PROTO/fish · https://proto.fish

fdroid:io.github.trevarj.motd.name: motd
fdroid:io.github.trevarj.motd.summary: Native IRC chat with history, themes, soju and ZNC support
fdroid:io.github.trevarj.motd.description:
motd is a native Android IRC client with a modern chat interface. Connect directly to IRC networks or use a soju or ZNC bouncer.
Features:
* Local message history and full-text search across chats or within one conversation, with jump-to-message
* Bouncer history and synchronized read markers where supported; soju multi-network management and ZNC playback
* Replies, reactions, typing indicators, nick autocomplete, and slash commands, depending on server capabilities
* Inline images, link previews including YouTube videos, and file uploads, with remote-media controls
* Chat folders, pinned chats, and an archive
* Material You dynamic color, curated themes, light, dark and AMOLED modes, adjustable text sizes, and message styles
* Builtin and custom-image wallpapers, including the System Crafters preset and selectable builtin outline colors
* TLS, SASL PLAIN and EXTERNAL, and client certificates
motd is Google-free and uses UnifiedPush for push delivery, not Firebase. Push requires a compatible server or bouncer and an installed UnifiedPush distributor. Persistent socket delivery is also available. Plain IRC networks retain local history; remote history, read-state sync and push depend on the server or bouncer.
Optional per-network routing supports SOCKS5, Tor through Orbot, and embedded VLESS with TCP + REALITY or WebSocket + TLS. Embedded VLESS requires a compatible proxy server and is limited to arm64-v8a. Routing is not a guarantee of anonymity.
An opt-in read-aloud feature uses installed Android offline voices. Third-party speech engines still receive the text they read.
Requires Android 8.0 or newer and a 64-bit ARM device.

fdroid:org.grating.recolldroid.name: RecollDroid
fdroid:org.grating.recolldroid.summary: UI for the Recoll fulltext search engine.
fdroid:org.grating.recolldroid.description:
RecollDroid is an Android front end to the Recoll full text search engine typically used
to index all of your desktop/server files. For more information on Recoll, see
https://www.recoll.org
RecollDroid consists of an andriod ui and a thin server layer providing a RestAPI interface
to the Recoll software. It uses Recoll's python API and supports multiple users securely
via basic auth over https.
The server layer makes use of FastAPI to provide the restful endpoints for the UI. It
contains no authentication code itself but depends on a proxying layer to ensure only
validated users can connect. The supported setup is to use the Nginx reverse proxy to
perform basic auth together with the unit app server to host the recoll rest api.

* Large, high-contrast heading display

fdroid:org.seishingakuen.shougibu.description:
Seishin Gakuen Shogi Club (清正学園将棋部) is a Shogi (Japanese chess) game played against an on-device AI, or against a friend on the same Wi-Fi (通信対戦). The app never connects to the internet.
 Features 
* Complete Shogi rules — check, nifu (double pawn), uchifuzume (pawn-drop mate), sennichite (repetition, including the perpetual-check loss) and nyuugyoku (entering-king, 27-point rule).
* Offline AI — an AlphaZero-style policy + value network (Bonanza-method trained) runs on-device through a single-threaded PUCT MCTS. Eight strength levels.
* Eight opponents — club members and teachers from Lv 1 to Lv 8, each with a portrait and a short bio.
* Your avatar — pick one of 16 students to stand for you. Your portrait sits under the board and changes expression with the game; in 通信対戦 your opponent sees it too.

* Teacher mode — tap "Ask Kato-sensei!" during a game to see the top three candidate moves with win rates. You still choose the move yourself.
* Play experience — multi-step undo, resign, last-move highlight, piece and UI sounds, haptics, save and resume.
* Kifu save and review — export games as .kif, then replay and analyse them from the title screen. Every move is evaluated by MCTS and tagged ◎ good / △ dubious / × blunder, with a recommended move for blunders.
* Board — kaya-style wood grain, traditional pentagonal pieces, brush-script piece kanji (Fude Goshirae).
The user interface is in Japanese.
 Privacy 
No ads, tracking or analytics. The AI model runs locally. The network permissions are used only for 通信対戦 (play against a friend on the same Wi-Fi); the app never contacts the internet.

flathub:io.github.Duecki1.CalibRaw.name: CalibRaw
flathub:io.github.Duecki1.CalibRaw.summary: Develop RAW photos with non-destructive editing
flathub:io.github.Duecki1.CalibRaw.description:
CalibRaw is a GPU-accelerated RAW photo editor. Browse your photo library, develop camera RAW
 files, and fine-tune color, tone, and detail in one workflow. Adjustments are saved in sidecar
 files so your original photos remain intact.
 Shape your images with tone curves, color wheels, and targeted color adjustments. Apply lens
 corrections, recover highlights, and combine bracketed exposures with HDR merge. Brush, gradient,
 and shape masks let you make local adjustments, while optional AI tools process masks, noise reduction,
 and object removal on your device after downloading their models.
 Develop RAW files from a wide range of cameras, including Fujifilm X-Trans sensors
 Adjust exposure, white balance, tone curves, and individual color ranges
 Correct lens distortion, chromatic aberration, and vignetting
 Apply local masks and creative effects with independent adjustments
 Export finished photos, including lossless JPEG XL images

 the GNOME desktop. It allows you to read, find and send email
 with a straightforward, modern interface.
 Conversations allow you to read a complete discussion without
 having to find and click from message to message.
 Geary’s features include:
 Quick email account setup
 Shows related messages together in conversations
 Fast, full text and keyword search
 Full-featured HTML and plain text message composer
 Desktop notification of new mail
 Compatible with GMail, Yahoo! Mail, Outlook.com and other IMAP servers

flathub:org.kde.kgeotag.name: KGeoTag
flathub:org.kde.kgeotag.description:
KGeoTag is a standalone geotagging program. Images can be associated with geographic coordinates
 by different means: On the one hand, a matching with GPX encoded geodata can be done, on the other
 hand, the coordinates can be set manually, either via drag and drop onto a map, via bookmarks or
 by manually supplying them. The coordinates can be stored in the images' Exif header and/or in
 XMP sidecar files.

fedora-packages:btrfs-backup-ng/btrfs-ba.description: btrfs-backup-ng creates, transfers, prunes and restores btrfs snapshots: to local disks, to other machines over SSH, or as raw send-stream files on any filesystem (NFS, SMB, cloud storage). It is configured with TOML and driven by subcommands such as run, snapshot, transfer, prune, restore and verify, with an interactive wizard to write the first configuration. Features: - Incremental transfers, with the parent matched by btrfs UUID so a re-created snapshot is never used as the wrong parent - Time-based retention: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly and yearly - Restore from local, SSH and raw targets, as full or incremental chains - Stream compression with zstd, gzip, lz4, xz, bzip2, lzop, pigz and pbzip2 - Raw backups with GPG or OpenSSL encryption and a checksummed metadata sidecar that raw verify can check - SSH host-key verification, bandwidth limits and sudo support on the remote - Locks kept on the remote target, so a prune running elsewhere cannot delete a snapshot that a restore is reading - Snapper integration, including restoring snapshots with their metadata - Import of btrbk configuration, snapshots and systemd timers - systemd timer installation, email and webhook notifications, and a doctor command that diagnoses and repairs common problems Man pages and bash, zsh and fish completions are included.

firefox-addons:3058060.name: Choice — Ethical Shopping
firefox-addons:3058060.summary: See sourced company actions on labor, environment, privacy and politics as you shop, plus alternatives. No account. Free.
firefox-addons:3058060.description:
Choice does not decide which companies are good or bad. You decide what matters to you.
Start with 15 plain Yes, No or Not sure questions covering labor, climate, privacy, political activity, civil rights and other company actions. Review or refine any answer from the larger searchable catalog whenever you want. Your answers stay in your browser; Choice never receives them.
When Choice has a published record for the company behind a site, it compares sourced actions with the values you selected on your device. A warning appears only when complete evidence conflicts with something you selected. Open it to see the action, actor, date, confidence and published source. Missing evidence stays unknown—it is never presented as a clean record. Alternatives must pass product-fit, ownership, evidence and improvement checks.
What it does:
• 15-question starter setup plus a searchable belief catalog
• Source-backed warnings only for your own explicit answers
• Exact action, actor, date and source behind each warning
• Evidence-aware alternatives, with unknown coverage labeled honestly
• No overall good/bad company grade or political compatibility score
• No account, no paid tier, no subscription and no advertising
Data choice before use:
Choice explains its domain check and waits for you to agree — at the end of setup, or the first time you open the popup. Before that affirmative choice, it reads no site domain and makes no operational network request. Pressing "Not now" keeps checks off. Disabling Choice stops every request; uninstalling also removes its stored data.
If allowed, Choice automatically sends only the visited site's bare registrable domain—for example, " amazon.com "—to youneedchoice.com over HTTPS to request an existing company record. This browsing activity is used only to retrieve the company record requested by the extension. Choice never sends the full URL, path, page content, searches, form data, your belief answers, an account, login, device ID, analytics cookie or advertising identifier. Cloudflare processes the bare-domain request and network metadata in transit to deliver and protect the service. Choice's origin access logs omit request bodies and client identity. An unknown domain is not saved or turned into a research job.
The extension sends no analytics, usage events or automatic error reports. Aggregate coverage is requested only after domain-check consent. Company-search text is sent when you use the extension's search. If you press a feedback control, Choice sends the company and finding identifiers, the reason you select and an optional bounded note; it attaches no account, device identifier, analytics cookie or session.

firefox-addons:3080562.name: Shop Addresses
firefox-addons:3080562.summary: Creates a unique e-mail address per online shop (e.g. m-gardenshop-2026-k3x9q2ab@your-domain) on your own mail server and fills it into the order form. Works with any server offering the shop address API, e.g. Roundcube with the identity_api plugin.
firefox-addons:3080562.description:
Give every online shop its own e-mail address – created on the fly, right in the checkout form.
When you focus an e-mail field, a small button appears. It suggests the shop name from the website (e.g. gardenshop.example → gardenshop), has your mail server create a new address like m-gardenshop-2026-k3x9q2ab@your-domain and fills it in, including “repeat e-mail” fields. Addresses you already created for a shop are offered for reuse. The toolbar popup (also on Android) and a context menu (desktop) do the same.
Why? You see which shop leaked or sold your address, and you can shut down a single address on the server.
Requirements:
• A mail server offering the shop address REST API (open specification), e.g. Roundcube 1.5–1.7 with the plugin identity_api: https://github.com/michael-dev/roundcube-identity_api 
• A personal access token from that server (in Roundcube under Settings → Preferences → Shop address API, one click with “Connect browser extension”)
Privacy: The extension only talks to the server whose API URL you configure. It sends your access token and the shop name and receives the generated address – nothing else leaves your browser, no analytics, no third parties. The user interface is in English and German.

apple-macos:6761687571.name: Audivella Audio Books
apple-macos:6761687571.description:
Every audiobook holds a world. For supported classics, Audivella's Story Atlas lets you see that world unfold as you listen.
Discover illustrated character portraits, memorable places, revealed facts, and the relationships that connect them. Your Atlas grows only with the chapters you have listened to, so future characters and plot details stay hidden until their time.
Open any person or place to explore a focused detail page with aliases, story context, revealed facts, connections, and their first appearance. When available, jump directly back to the moment an entry first appeared in the audiobook.
Story Atlas is designed to make classic stories easier to follow without turning them into spoilers. It is especially helpful for books with large casts, changing locations, and relationships that develop over many chapters.
Atlas works alongside Audivella's complete listening experience:
- Spoiler-safe character and place discovery
- Illustrated portraits aligned with each book's visual style
- Character facts and relationship maps revealed through listening
- Detailed person and place pages
- First-appearance navigation
- Chapter downloads for offline playback
- Voice options, bookmarks, and saved progress
- Background audio and system playback controls
- Reading insights, suggestions, and reminders
Listen naturally, reveal the story, and return to your Atlas whenever you want to remember who is who and how the world connects.
